traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Malpighiaceae: leaves usually opposite, rarely alternate; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate; stipules present or absent; plants usually hermaphrodite, rarely polygamous; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody; flowers in panicles, in cymes, in racemes or in umbels; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit drupe, nut, samara, aggregate or schizocarp; parts of each whorl 5; stamens 5 to 10; carpels (2-) 3 (-5). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Malpighiaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add whorled (rarely): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 312: subopposite or ternate.
